stem: A nurse is monitoring the head growth of a healthy 4-month-old infant in the United States. Which reference should be used to plot head circumference over time?

options.A: WHO head-circumference-for-age growth standards for children from birth to 2 years
options.C: CDC BMI-for-age charts for children 2 years and older
options.D: A single fixed newborn head-circumference range used for all infants regardless of age and sex

rationale: CDC and AAP recommend WHO Child Growth Standards for U.S. children from birth to 2 years. These include sex-specific head-circumference-for-age charts and are used to track growth over time. A fixed newborn range is not an appropriate longitudinal standard, and BMI-for-age charts are not the head-circumference reference for an infant. Growth charts contribute to the overall clinical assessment and are not stand-alone diagnostic instruments. Therefore A is the best answer.
educational_objective: Use WHO head-circumference-for-age growth standards to monitor head growth in U.S. infants from birth through 2 years rather than relying on a single universal centimeter range.
